{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Bright Visual Only", "Combined", "Dim Visual Only", "ICMS Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation yields the poorest performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (0.273), longest Time-to-Target (4.682 s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.737 units/s), and lowest Angular Dispersion (0.236).",
    "Combined stimulation produces the highest Success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.562 s), with strong Path Efficiency (0.502) and Average Speed (12.833 units/s), plus the highest AD (0.399).",
    "Bright Visual Only achieves the second-highest Success rate (0.785), comparable to Combined, with slightly lower Average Speed (12.679 units/s) and AD (0.387) than Combined.",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance: Success rates of 0.673 and 0.685 respectively, Time-to-Target around 3.0-3.1 s, and similar Path Efficiency (~0.43) and Average Speed (~12.0 units/s).",
    "Angular Dispersion follows a clear hierarchy: Combined > Bright Visual Only > ICMS Only > Dim Visual Only > Sham, suggesting more variable movement patterns with richer stimulation.",
    "Sample sizes vary substantially across paradigms, with Combined dominating (n=48,846) versus Sham being smallest (n=3,505)."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined (0.780) and Bright Visual Only (0.785) shows a massive ~50 percentage point gap, the largest absolute difference across any metric.",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.682 s) is 83% slower than Combined (2.562 s) and 79% slower than Bright Visual Only (2.614 s).",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502) represents a 63% relative improvement with stimulation.",
    "Average Speed: Sham (10.737 units/s) is 16-20% slower than all active stimulation conditions.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): Sham (0.236) versus Combined (0.399) shows a 69% increase in movement variability with combined stimulation.",
    "Dim versus Bright Visual Only: Bright Visual Only substantially outperforms Dim Visual Only on Success (+11.1 points), Time-to-Target (-0.526 s), and Path Efficiency (+0.069)."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Any form of sensory stimulation dramatically improves mouse navigation performance compared to Sham, with visual stimulation appearing particularly effective. Bright visual cues match or slightly exceed combined ICMS+visual stimulation on Success rate, suggesting visual information may be the dominant driver of performance. The low Angular Dispersion in Sham indicates more stereotyped, possibly less exploratory or more direct but inefficient movement patterns, while higher AD with stimulation suggests more active, varied trajectory exploration that nonetheless achieves targets faster. Dim visual stimulation underperforms bright visual stimulation, indicating stimulus salience matters. The large effect sizes between Sham and active conditions suggest robust experimental manipulation, though the dominance of the Combined condition in sample size warrants caution in direct comparisons.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes across paradigms (Combined n=48,846 vs Sham n=3,505) may affect comparison reliability and generalizability.",
    "No statistical tests (ANOVA, post-hoc comparisons, confidence intervals) are provided to assess significance of observed differences.",
    "Missing information on experimental design: whether paradigms were blocked, randomized, or counterbalanced within mice; whether order effects exist.",
    "No breakdown by individual mice to assess within-subject consistency versus between-subject variability.",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme maximum value (29.817) suggesting potential outliers that may distort means; median values would be informative.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion) interpretation as 'more variable movement' versus 'more exploratory' is inferential without trajectory visualization.",
    "No information on task difficulty, target distance, or whether metrics are comparable across trials."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects models with Mouse as random effect to account for within-mouse clustering, followed by pairwise comparisons with Tukey or Bonferroni correction to identify statistically significant differences between paradigms. Visualize distributions (boxplots, violin plots) to assess normality and outlier influence on means. Calculate effect sizes (Cohen's d) for all pairwise comparisons. Perform sensitivity analysis excluding extreme Path Efficiency outliers. If trial-level data available, examine learning curves and trial-by-trial dynamics. Finally, consider a variance components analysis to quantify how much variance is attributable to Mouse versus Stim Paradigm versus residual error."
}
